As of 2021, the company has a total of 1,122 outlets and collection centers across India and parts of [[Nepal]], [[Bangladesh]] and the [[Middle East]].{{cite web|title=Thyrocare Technologies profit, revenue, etc!|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/thyrocare-technologies-ltd/yearly/companyid-60244.cms|website=economictimes.indiatimes.com|publisher=The economic times India|accessdate=30 June 2021|date=30 June 2021}} On 26 June 2021, Indian e-pharmacy and online healthcare aggregator [[PharmEasy]]'s parent API Holdings acquired a 66.1% controlling stake in Thyrocare,{{Cite web|last=Dhanjal|first=Swaraj Singh|date=2021-06-25|title=PharmEasy to acquire 66% stake in diagnostic chain Thyrocare for ₹4,500 cr|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/pharmeasy-to-acquire-66-stake-in-diagnostic-chain-thyrocare-for-rs-4500-cr-11624627214297.html|access-date=2021-09-01|website=mint|language=en}} making Thyrocare the first Indian listed company to be acquired by a startup.{{Cite web|title=PharmEasy opens up quicker public listing options with its acquisition of Thyrocare|url=https://www.businessinsider.in/business/startups/news/pharmeasy-opens-up-quicker-public-listing-options-with-its-acquisition-of-thyrocare/articleshow/83922011.cms|access-date=2021-07-03|website=Business Insider}}{{Cite web|title=PharmEasy To Acquire 66.1% Stake In Thyrocare For Rs 4,546 Crore|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/pharmeasy-to-acquire-66-1-stake-in-thyrocare-for-rs-4546-crore-7088951.html|access-date=2021-07-03|website=Moneycontrol|date=25 June 2021 }}{{Cite web|last=Datta|first=PT Jyothi|title=PharmEasy buys out Thyrocare for ₹4,546 cr|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/pharmeasy-buys-out-thyrocare-for-4546-cr/article34978562.ece|access-date=2021-07-03|website=@businessline|date=25 June 2021 |language=en}} == History == [[File:Thyrocare Logo.png|thumb|Old logo of Thyrocare]] Thyrocare was started in 1996, by [[Arokiaswamy Velumani|A. Velumani]], a former scientist at [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] (BARC) in [[Mumbai]]. The first laboratory was set up in [[Byculla]], Mumbai, with an initial focus on [[Thyroid function tests|thyroid testing]].{{cite web|title=Thyrocare Technologies: Testing new waters in medical diagnostics, Hidden Gems|url=http://forbesindia.com/article/hidden-gems/thyrocare-technologies-testing-new-waters-in-medical-diagnostics/41051/1|website=forbesindia.com|accessdate=24 September 2016|date=10 September 2015}} The laboratory was later shifted to a larger set-up, its main headquarters and central processing laboratory at [[Navi Mumbai]]. The company introduced a franchisee model for procuring samples to be sent for testing at their central laboratory in Mumbai. In 2010, Thyrocare raised its first [[private equity]] funding of {{INR}}188 crore from New Delhi-based CX Partners in exchange for a 30% stake.{{cite web|title=A panacea for the masses|url=http://www.thesmartceo.in/growth-enterprise/a-panacea-for-the-masses.html|website=thesmartceo.in|publisher=The Smart CEO|access-date=15 September 2016|date=1 December 2012}} It set up a subsidiary, Nuclear Healthcare Limited, which uses PET-CT to detect and locate cancerous cells.{{cite web|title=Thyrocare: Strong base, multiple new triggers|url=http://smartinvestor.business-standard.com/market/story-380304-storydet-Thyrocare_Strong_base_multiple_new_triggers.htm#.V6LDydJ97IV|website=SmartInvestor.in|publisher=SmartInvestor|access-date=16 September 2016|date=26 April 2016}}{{cite web|title=Nueclear Healthcare Limited Secures INR 22 Crores From Norwest Venture Partners (NVP)|url=http://www.marketwired.com/press-release/nueclear-healthcare-limited-secures-inr-22-crores-from-norwest-venture-partners-nvp-1747210.htm|website=marketwired|access-date=16 September 2016|date=18 January 2013}} In 2014, [[Siemens Healthcare]]'s diagnostic division installed its world's largest laboratory automation track – Aptio Automation – at its laboratory in Mumbai.{{cite web|title=Siemens installs 'Aptio automation solution' lab at Thyrocare, Diagnostics|url=http://www.pharmabiz.com/NewsDetails.aspx?aid=83090&sid=2|website=Pharmabiz.com|access-date=16 September 2016|date=22 July 2014}} In April 2016, Thyrocare made its [[initial public offering]] (IPO),{{cite news|title=Thyrocare Technologies IPO draws huge response, subscribed 73.24x|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/ipos/fpos/thyrocare-technologies-ipo-draws-huge-response-subscribed-73-24x/articleshow/52037618.cms|accessdate=16 September 2016|publisher=ET Markets|date=30 April 2016}} and became the second diagnostic firm in India to be listed on BSE and NSE. In 2021, [[PharmEasy]] parent API Holdings acquired a 66.1% stake in Thyrocare.{{Cite web|title=EXCLUSIVE {{!}} API Holdings' Acquisition Of Thyrocare Will Create One-stop Shop For Healthcare Solutions, Says PharmEasy's Siddharth Shah|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/mergers-acquisitions/exclusive-pharmeasys-parent-api-holdings-to-acquire-thyrocare-to-create-one-stop-shop-for-healthcare-solutions-siddharth-shah-pharmeasy-7089421.html|access-date=2021-12-09|website=Moneycontrol|date=25 June 2021 |language=en}} In 2023, Thyrocare integrated [[Artificial intelligence|AI]]-based devices to automate manual microscopy across its network with SigTuple's AI100.{{cite web | url=https://health.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/diagnostics/thyrocare-to-automate-manual-microscopy-across-its-network-with-sigtuples-ai100/98170440 | title=Thyrocare to automate manual microscopy across its network with SigTuple's AI100 - ET HealthWorld }} ==Services== Thyrocare initially started with thyroid testing but now has more than 350 tests and packages, along with 83 odd profiles comprising different tests for preventive care and wellness under its brand Aarogyam.{{cite web|title=Thyrocare: Strong base, multiple new triggers|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/thyrocare-strong-base-multiple-new-triggers-116042500908_1.html|publisher=Business Standard|accessdate=15 September 2016|date=25 April 2016}} During the peak of [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Thyrocare carried out more than 8 [[lakh]] tests per month.{{citation needed|date=May 2024}} Thyrocare's 68% of business comes from the DSA model to promote its services.{{citation needed|date=May 2024}} ==Controversies== In April 2020, [[Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation]] issued a [[show cause notice]] to Thyrocare over lapses in its [[COVID-19 testing|testing of COVID-19 samples]] and ordered the company to stop testing as "incomplete or wrong information about patients were found in the reports".{{cite news |title=BMC Asks Thyrocare to Stop Testing for Coronavirus Over 'Serious' Lapses in Patients' Reports |url=https://www.news18.com/news/india/bmc-asks-thyrocare-to-stop-testing-for-coronavirus-over-serious-lapses-in-patients-reports-2596259.html |access-date=10 February 2023 |work=News18 |date=28 April 2020 |language=en}} In May 2020, [[Panvel Municipal Corporation]] ordered Thyrocare to stop testing samples in Panvel city limits as the lab was producing false positive reports.{{cite news |last1=Assainar |first1=Raina |title=PMC orders Thyrocare not to test swab samples |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mumbai/pmc-orders-thyrocare-not-to-test-swab-samples/article31569608.ece |access-date=10 February 2023 |work=The Hindu |date=12 May 2020 |language=en-IN}} In June 2020, the [[Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation]] demanded cancellation of Thyrocare's registration after discrepancies in the lab's report led to a patient's death,{{cite news |title=NMMC: Scrap registration of lab for fiasco |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/nmmc-scrap-registration-of-lab-for-fiasco/articleshow/76252624.cms |access-date=10 February 2023 |work=The Times of India |date=8 June 2020}} while [[Thane Municipal Corporation]] banned Thyrocare in the city for producing false positive reports.{{cite news |last1=Pathak |first1=Kalpana |last2=Leo |first2=Leroy |title=Mumbai's ban on two labs to hit covid-19 testing in the city |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/mumbai-s-ban-on-two-labs-to-hit-covid-19-testing-in-the-city-11591979197655.html |access-date=10 February 2023 |work=mint |date=12 June 2020 |language=en}} In July 2020, a Thyrocare lab in [[Pune]] was banned from conducting COVID-19 tests after producing false positive reports.{{cite news |title=Pvt lab botches result, banned from nCoV tests |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/pune/pvt-lab-botches-result-banned-from-ncov-tests/articleshow/76930235.cms |access-date=10 February 2023 |work=The Times of India |date=13 July 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} [[Category:Laboratories in India]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1996]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of Thyrocare Technologies Limited is an Indian multinational chain of diagnostic and preventive care laboratories, headquartered in Navi Mumbai. As of 2021, the company has a total of 1,122 outlets and collection centers across India and parts of Nepal, Bangladesh and the Middle East.
On 26 June 2021, Indian e-pharmacy and online healthcare aggregator PharmEasy's parent API Holdings acquired a 66.1% controlling stake in Thyrocare, making Thyrocare the first Indian listed company to be acquired by a startup.
